As a Defence team, we wanted to ask the Trial Chamber to make a ruling as regards the communication between parties and the witness. So we do believe it's an issue of principle which concerns the procedure. After the witness has begun to testify under oath, we think that he could no longer be approached by any of the parties except pursuant to an authorisation by the Trial Chamber. This same ruling was made in the Kupreskic case, in paragraph 18 of the relevant decision. From what I have heard from my learned colleagues from the Prosecution, I do not believe that they will have any objections, but let them say so if that is indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Harmon. What is your position as regards this application by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President and Your Honours; good afternoon, counsel. Mr. Visnjic and I talked about this earlier. In principle, we have no objection to that insofar as it relates to substantive discussions relating to the testimony. However, we need to occasionally see how the witness is doing, how his transportation is being arranged, and in the course of everyday contact with witnesses, we need to be able to have those minimal contacts that don't discuss or touch upon the testimony at all. In principle, we have absolutely no objection to a lack of communication, after the direct-examination is concluded, on substantive matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, the contact that you have mentioned as necessary contact after the witness has been sworn in, couldn't that contact be made through the unit for protection of witnesses and victims? Is it not the task of that particular unit to assist the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. We also coordinate with the Victims and Witnesses Unit in making those arrangements. So members of my staff will be, I'm quite sure, in the presence of and possibly communicate with these witnesses. That's a detail that I don't get involved with. However, I have an assistant who works closely with the Victims and Witnesses Unit and does have contact with these people. I know that my assistant does not deal in substantive matters with these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have a moment to consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Judge Wald has a question for you. Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, you've heard Mr. Harmon's reply to your motion, and I think there's obviously agreement there should be no contact dealing with the substantive testimony once it has begun. Do you have objections, nonetheless, to his condition that sometimes it's necessary to confer with the witness about the logistics, and would it satisfy you if in such case the Prosecution told you they were going to have contact about logistics so you would know about that, or be present, if you wanted?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the problem couldn't be resolved in any other way, or if the issues of logistics cannot be tackled in any other way, we agree to this type of communication, the way you have just described it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harmon, how does that sound to you, that if such an occasion arises that you need a logistic communication and coordination of the Victims and Witnesses Protection Unit, that you notify the Defence that you're going to have such a -- does that pose problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It does not. We're satisfied with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, you may sit down. Thank you very much. Mr. Visnjic, before we make a ruling, I should like to know whether you are requesting this because one other Chamber has made a ruling to that effect, or is it because you have some very specific reason for doing so?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we do not have any specific reasons for that. We just wanted the matter to be settled in a formal way, so that in future we do not encounter problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Harmon, you told us that you had already spoken amongst yourselves about that. Is it some kind of a prevention or have there been any problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm unaware of any problems whatsoever. Mr. Visnjic approached me this morning, and my colleagues, and said that he was going to raise the issue as a matter of principle with the Chamber, and we said we understood that, and we agreed to the issues that he was going to raise with the Chamber. The only exception I would ask, at this point, should the Court rule that way, is that we be permitted to explain that to this witness, who is finding himself, at this point in time, in a situation where there may have been some anticipation of having a conversation of some kind after the session was over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't think I have understood properly your question, Mr. Harmon. It's probably my fault. Could you please be so kind and repeat what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think the issue that I raised with the Chamber can be resolved should the Court make the ruling that Mr. Visnjic has requested. This witness, if he could be informed of the reasons why we will not have contact with him after the court session today, that would clarify the issues for this particular witness, who finds himself in the middle of this debate. The other point of clarification I would like to make is I take it, under Mr. Visnjic's motion, the Prosecutor's Office, at the conclusion of the testimony, can have contact with the witness. We traditionally do that, just to say, "Thank you for coming from Bosnia," and, "Goodbye and have a safe journey." So if that could be clarified, we would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do you have something else, Mr. Visnjic? Anything else you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should merely like to announce that on Monday, I shall have to raise two more issues. There is no time for this now. So on Monday, in the beginning when we start, before the witness comes in, we shall need to raise some other issues, but it won't take more than half an hour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another issue, Mr. Harmon, is that we should like to know where are we as regards the next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thus far, Mr. President, we are close to the schedule that we had sketched out for ourselves. Next week we have the testimonies of approximately 14 witnesses scheduled. We did not anticipate today that this particular witness would carry over, so that will cause our schedule to move, advance a little bit, but we are, I'm told by the people who are responsible for contacting and moving the witnesses here, that we have a full week next week and that we will advance -- we hope to advance very quickly through the testimonies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the following weeks until the May the 2nd, that is, end of April, could you tell us something about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can. We have sketched out a number of testimonies that carry us through April the 14th, and it is our anticipation that we will carry through. I haven't calculated the number of our total number of witnesses who will have testified, but if you give me just a minute, I can make a fairly decent calculation at that by counting the number of witnesses on my planning through the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, but the Chamber wishes to know -- because as you know, there is the question of filling in the two weeks which were formally assigned to another case. So you say that we shall have witnesses for the next week. That is so, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, we have witnesses scheduled through April the 14th, as the schedule initially indicated, then there was a hiatus, and we have not then planned for the following -- I think it was a two-week session that was scheduled next. I'd have to look at my scheduled, but we have not planned for the witnesses for the next segment after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Even if you do not have witnesses envisaged for those weeks, we shall have enough witnesses until the 14th, and you will be able also to think about planning for the next period, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You may be seated, Mr. Harmon. Thank you very much. As for the motion of the Defence and the Prosecution, the Chamber will make an oral decision on Monday. I should like to remind you that we shall be back here next Monday at 9.30, and we shall then have the opportunity to hear the issues which the Defence wishes to raise. At present, I turn to the witness to tell him that we have indeed done all that we could to set you free today. Unfortunately, we have not managed to do that, and you will have to spend your weekend here and to continue giving your evidence next Monday. I believe there are no further issues. I merely need to tell you that next week Judge Wald will not be with us for three days of the next week so that the Chamber will sit in two. Judge Riad and myself will be sitting. We already know the conditions, which are the conditions of Rule 15 bis of the Rules. Thank you. If there are no other matters. I should like to adjourn. I apologise for the slight delay. Thank you. Nice weekend to all of you. We shall meet back on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 2.37 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of March, 2000 at 9.30 a.m.
